raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, points $A$, $P$, and $T$ lie on the circle $\odot O$, $OT\perp TB$, the arc $\overset{\frown}{AT}$ measures $60^\circ$, the radius of $\odot O$ is 2, $TB=2$, point $B$ and point $A$ are on opposite sides of line $OT$, $PB$ intersects $\odot O$ at point $C$. When $\angle APB=60^\circ$, what is the value of $\angle PBT$? What is the length of $BC$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution}: Connect $OA$, $OC$, $TC$, and draw $CD\perp TB$ at point $C$ with foot $D$. 
$\because \angle APB=60^\circ$, 
$\therefore \angle AOC=2\angle APC=120^\circ$, 
$\because$ the degree of $\overset{\frown}{AT}$ is $60^\circ$, 
$\therefore \angle AOT=60^\circ$, 
$\therefore \angle TOC=\angle AOC-\angle AOT=60^\circ$, 
$\because OT=OC$, 
$\therefore \triangle OTC$ is an equilateral triangle, 
$\therefore TC=OT=OC=2$, and $\angle OTC=60^\circ$, 
$\because OT\perp TB$, 
$\therefore \angle OTB=90^\circ$, 
$\therefore \angle CTB=\angle OTB-\angle OTC=30^\circ$, 
$\because TC=TB=2$, 
$\therefore \angle PBT=\angle TCB=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-\angle CTB\right)=75^\circ$, 
In $\triangle TCD$ right-angled at $D$, $\angle CTB=30^\circ$, $TC=2$, 
$\therefore CD=\frac{1}{2}TC=1$, $TD=\sqrt{3}CD=\sqrt{3}$, 
$\therefore BD=TB-TD=2-\sqrt{3}$, 
$\therefore CB=\sqrt{CD^{2}+DB^{2}}=\sqrt{1^{2}+(2-\sqrt{3})^{2}}=\sqrt{8-4\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{8-2\sqrt{12}}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})^{2}}=\boxed{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}$.
